html:
SMTO-BOOT-0030 — The installer found a vLLM download from an unexpected place

GUID: 22620349-0e47-49cc-8d77-c11343c8433b
Slug: boot-vllm-wheel-origin-rejected
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The installer only downloads vLLM from the official vLLM release page. The newest release pointed to a download somewhere else, so the installer refused it and stopped before installing vLLM.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Copy the full terminal output from this install attempt, including the SMTO-BOOT-0030 line and the "CPU:" and "GPU" lines above it. It shows your hardware and where the installer stopped, which the maintainer needs to check the release.
  2. Send it to the person who maintains your SMTO copy and ask them to check the vLLM release and the installer. The error alone does not establish whether the unexpected download is safe, so a person has to check it.
  3. Before installing again, run conda env list. If the environment name from this attempt is listed, use a new name or remove that half-built environment first. The download was refused after the environment was created, so that name is already taken by an environment without vLLM.

What success looks like

  • After the release or installer is fixed, the installer prints "Selected vLLM" and installs from the official release page.

If it still fails

  • Keep the terminal output and send it to the person who maintains your SMTO copy. Don't download or install a vLLM package from another website to get around this; the installer blocked it on purpose.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • select_wheel rejected a matching GitHub release asset whose browser_download_url does not start with https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/releases/download/, aborting the plan before any vLLM package was downloaded.

What this means

  • A non-PyPI release candidate's browser_download_url does not start with the accepted vLLM GitHub release-download prefix. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • A non-PyPI release candidate's browser_download_url does not start with the accepted vLLM GitHub release-download prefix.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the candidate's actual release metadata; the check does not prove that a network redirect occurred.

How to fix it

  • Fetch https://api.github.com/repos/vllm-project/vllm/releases/tags/ with v and the latest PyPI version appended, inspect the assets' browser_download_url values, and report the unexpected origin; keep the prefix restriction in select_wheel. Remove the partially created environment or use a new name before reinstalling.
  • Verify the exact upstream candidate URL and report unexpected release metadata; preserve the accepted-origin restriction.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected candidate has a verified accepted upstream release location.

What not to do

  • Do not delete evidence or invent a configuration change for an unexplained internal failure.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
